events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The trip is RydeX, a fixed-fare (non-metered) service: the fare was quoted at booking and mileage during the trip does not change it [F4][F6][RD-2]. F6 breaks the $34.38 down into base $3.90, distance $23.39, time $5.62, platform $1.47 — all published components — and there is no unpublished add-on, no ERP/toll or waiting charge, and no surge [F5][F6][FARE-1]. This matches the rider's own complaint that the meter came to 16.6 km, not "17 km" as the app estimated.

One off-route segment is established: 09:06–09:13, 4.84 km driven where the optimal route covers 0 km, up to 1176 m off route [F3], against an overall +5.0 km / +30% and +11.1 min [F1][F2]. The segment is not exempted by any incident on the replaced stretch: no qualifying traffic incident was recorded in the trip window and speed bands alone do not exempt [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. There is also no rider-requested named stop in the record [F7][F8][RD-3].

The driver's excuse is that his GPS rerouted him [F10], which is no reasonable cause under RD-1 and certainly no rider consent under RD-5 — a claim of agreement appearing only in the driver's post-trip statement is not consent, and the chat before the segment contains nothing but pickup logistics (rider at the main entrance in a blue shirt; driver arriving in 2 min in a white Honda Vezel) [F7][F8][F10][RD-5][RD-1]. So RD-1's shortest-and-most-direct obligation was breached on that segment.

That breach, however, produced no chargeable overcharge. For a non-metered service RD-2 refunds only ERP/toll actually incurred on the unexempt segment or undisclosed post-trip add-ons; here the billed distance 16.6 km does not exceed the optimal route 16.6 km [F4], and the fare components are all published [F6]. Refundable amount is therefore $0 → no_action, with the driver's RD-1 breach recorded [RD-2][FARE-1].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this is not a "repeated" breach and no flag_account is warranted [F16][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver statement in full — they contain only pickup arrangements and a fare disagreement, with no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]; safety_concern = none.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked into your fare dispute and are not issuing a refund. RydeX is a fixed-fare service: your price was set when you booked, so the distance shown after the trip does not change what you pay. We checked your bill and it breaks down entirely into the standard published fares, with no extra or hidden charges, and the distance billed was not more than the shortest route. So there is nothing to refund. You can still see the full breakdown in your trip receipt. Thanks for flagging it — your report was recorded.

DRIVER: We reviewed a route complaint on one of your RydeX trips. We found you drove a stretch that was not the shortest, most direct way to the destination, which is a breach of your route obligation. We are recording this on your file for pattern monitoring. There is no fare adjustment, no money owed either way, and no action against your account. Please follow the app's suggested route unless the rider asks otherwise. Repeated breaches could affect your account standing, so treat this as a warning.
